items.title: How do I use only the external display with my MacBook Pro lid open on Lion?
items.x_text:
❓ How do I use only the external display with my MacBook Pro lid open on Lion?

✅ Use Terminal command sudo nvram boot-args= iog=0x0 to enable external display.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=skD9ZFu-d9k
#COSMOS #macos

discovery.short_answer: Use Terminal command sudo nvram boot-args= iog=0x0 to enable external display.
discovery.full_answer: On Mac OS X Lion, to use only an external display with your MacBook Pro lid open, you can change a system setting via Terminal. Enter the command 'sudo nvram boot-args= iog=0x0' to revert to the behavior before Lion, which allows using just the external display while the lid is open. If you want to undo this change later, you can either reset the parameter with 'sudo nvram -d boot-args' or reset the PRAM by pressing Cmd+Option+P+R during startup. This method modifies the boot arguments stored in NVRAM to control display behavior.
discovery.grok_perspective: Caution is warranted when applying unverified terminal modifications to display settings on legacy macOS versions such as Lion, since results can differ by hardware and may impact stability.

youtube.title: Apple: nvram boot-args to boot in target disk mode

items.title: What is the origin and reason for Sheldon s triple knock in The Big Bang Theory?
items.x_text:
❓ What is the origin and reason for Sheldon s triple knock in The Big Bang Theory?

✅ Sheldon knocks thrice to avoid walking in on private moments.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AkZ0wEd7Nmc
#COSMOS #character

discovery.short_answer: Sheldon knocks thrice to avoid walking in on private moments.
discovery.full_answer: In The Big Bang Theory episode 'The Hot Tub Contamination,' the origin of Sheldon's triple knock is revealed. When Sheldon was 13, he came home early expecting the house to be empty but heard noises from his parents' bedroom. Upon opening the door, he discovered his father with another woman. This experience led Sheldon to develop the habit of knocking three times before entering a room. The first knock is a traditional signal, while the second and third knocks serve as warnings to allow people time to get dressed or prepare for someone's entrance. This ritual helps Sheldon avoid accidentally intruding on private or intimate moments.
discovery.grok_perspective: In the series, Sheldon's knocking pattern forms part of his established character habits. Its specific origin stays internal to the show's narrative without external confirmation.

items.title: “Your paper will be rejected if a reviewer can generate a better paper by using LLMs.”
items.x_text:
❓ “Your paper will be rejected if a reviewer can generate a better paper by using LLMs.”

✅ No, papers are not rejected for being outperformed by LLM-generated work.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q7cbfwoElXM
#COSMOS #publications

discovery.short_answer: No, papers are not rejected for being outperformed by LLM-generated work.
discovery.full_answer: In computer science conferences, the review process follows strict rules focusing solely on the submitted paper itself. Reviewers do not compare submissions to papers generated by large language models (LLMs) or use LLM outputs as a benchmark. The purpose of peer review is to assess the quality and contribution of the submitted work, not to evaluate it against AI-generated alternatives. Additionally, many venues prohibit fully LLM-generated papers, so such submissions are generally not publishable. Therefore, the claim that a paper will be rejected if a reviewer can produce a better paper using LLMs is not aligned with standard review practices.
discovery.grok_perspective: Rejection decisions hinge on factors like novelty, rigor, and clarity, which could indirectly intersect with LLM capabilities but lack established direct linkage in current practices. Policies may shift as tools evolve, warranting ongoing attention to guidelines.

youtube.title: How to Peer Review a Paper with AI — Novelty, Reports, Meta-Review

items.title: When was the American War of Independence first called a Revolution ?
items.x_text:
❓ When was the American War of Independence first called a Revolution ?

✅ The American War of Independence was called a Revolution from 1776.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gzALIXcY4pg
#COSMOS #historiography

discovery.short_answer: The American War of Independence was called a Revolution from 1776.
discovery.full_answer: The term 'Revolution' was used to describe the American War of Independence from its early stages. As early as April 1776, figures like William Henry Drayton explicitly referred to it as a revolution, drawing parallels to the earlier English Glorious Revolution of 1688. Thomas Paine also praised the conflict as a 'revolution' in 1778, highlighting its virtuous nature. By 1779, the Continental Congress published works titled with the term 'American Revolution,' indicating official recognition. Although some contemporaries viewed the conflict as a British civil war, the term 'Revolution' became the dominant way Americans referred to the war by its conclusion, replacing earlier references such as the Glorious Revolution.
discovery.grok_perspective: Historical nomenclature often evolved gradually through contemporary documents, making any single origin date inherently tentative without exhaustive archival review. Usage likely varied by region and author.

items.title: What is the most extreme weather found on another planet?
items.x_text:
❓ What is the most extreme weather found on another planet?

✅ HD 189733b has the most extreme known weather with molten glass rain.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gwl2dSyZNUw
#COSMOS #exoplanet

discovery.short_answer: HD 189733b has the most extreme known weather with molten glass rain.
discovery.full_answer: The exoplanet HD 189733b exhibits some of the most extreme weather conditions known outside our Solar System. Its atmosphere reaches temperatures over 1000°C, accompanied by incredibly strong winds traveling at about 7000 kilometers per hour. Remarkably, it experiences rain made of molten glass that falls sideways due to these fierce winds. Another planet, HD 80606 b, may have even faster winds—up to 3 miles per second—caused by rapid heating during its eccentric orbit, but these winds are not continuous and it does not have molten glass rain. Therefore, HD 189733b is considered a prime example of extreme extraterrestrial weather due to the combination of its high temperatures, intense wind speeds, and unusual precipitation.
discovery.grok_perspective: Assessing claims of extreme planetary weather depends heavily on limited observational data and how "extreme" is defined across varying atmospheric conditions. Indirect measurements often leave room for alternative interpretations of such phenomena.

youtube.title: Molten Glass Rain? The Wild Weather of HD 189733b! #shorts #short

items.title: What factors discouraged the Nazis from focusing all their forces on the Caucasus region during Operation Barbarossa?
items.x_text:
❓ What factors discouraged the Nazis from focusing all their forces on the Caucasus region during Operation?

✅ Diversion to Stalingrad and Leningrad weakened Caucasus focus.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o4bJ8GBcv08
#COSMOS #caucasus

discovery.short_answer: Diversion to Stalingrad and Leningrad weakened Caucasus focus.
discovery.full_answer: During Operation Barbarossa, the initial plan aimed at a broad advance to the Archangelsk-Astrakhan line, including the Caucasus region. However, after failing to capture Moscow in 1941 and facing Soviet counterattacks, Hitler shifted focus southward in 1942 with Fall Blau, targeting the Caucasus. Despite this, successes in the south led Hitler to divert forces to capture Stalingrad and later to move the 11th Army north to attack Leningrad. This diversion split the forces originally intended for the Caucasus, reducing their strength by about half. The capture of Voronezh and rapid progress along the Don encouraged Hitler to gamble on taking Stalingrad, which was strategically important on the Volga River. These decisions diluted the effort in the Caucasus, preventing a concentrated offensive there.
discovery.grok_perspective: Strategic priorities in Operation Barbarossa involved multiple simultaneous objectives across a vast front, which may have constrained any singular regional emphasis such as the Caucasus. Historical interpretations of these decisions remain subject to ongoing debate.
